assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty are a clean, original and transformative advance in precision measurement: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea removed Doppler and recoil shifts for many atoms at once, enabling the stability and accuracy that now underpins redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the early strontium clocks; Ye's JILA group brought the approach to the 10^-18 level and to many-body, spin-squeezed and resolved-gravitational-redshift regimes. A two-person prize is natural; other single-ion and Al+ clock groups (and the comb work already honoured in 2005) are separate threads that could be argued as omitted.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: many independent groups (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others) have confirmed 10^-18 performance and clock comparisons are routine; the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition is timely, and the work is a direct continuation of a field the prize has honoured before.
uncertainties: Whether ion-clock work (Wineland-related, 2012) and the optical-clock community's other contributors make a two-name credit look incomplete.
Whether the committee sees this as incremental in precision rather than a new concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a whole class of quantum matter classified by topology without a magnetic field; the theory is original, conceptually deep and has had far-reaching impact on materials, quantum transport and later topological phases.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The credited three is a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration, but BHZ (and Zhang) and the 3D topological insulator discoveries complicate the credit boundary.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the quantum spin Hall edge states, 3D topological insulators and many materials have been confirmed by multiple independent groups for more than fifteen years, and the Nobel Committee has already recognised topological phase transitions (2016), so timing is good though the field is no longer new.
uncertainties: Competing credit to Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and to Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents for the 3D case.
Practical applications remain limited compared with the conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created an entirely new tunable platform for correlated and superconducting flat-band physics; the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 experiments showed correlated insulators and superconductivity, launching moire quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery. Cao and the MIT group members are not in the credited set, and Dean/Kim/Yacoby groups' contemporaneous work and Dean's hBN-based devices overlap, so allocation is arguable but the three-name set is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: the key results have been reproduced by many groups and spawned fractional Chern insulators and related effects, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still evolving, so some may feel it is slightly early.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconducting pairing remains unsettled.
Credit for the experimental side (junior co-authors and parallel groups) is uncertain.
Dependence on hBN encapsulation (candidate B017) is a compound-discovery question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned the Hubbard model into an experimentally controllable system, with the superfluid-Mott transition, quantum gas microscopy and later studies of many-body dynamics; it is a deep and clearly original advance bridging AMO and condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch-Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, and Greiner-Bloch observed the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition; Bloch and Greiner later developed quantum gas microscopes, and Esslinger the fermionic work. The five credited names exceed what a prize can hold, so I choose the proposal-plus-experiment core; the omission of Jaksch, Cirac and Esslinger would be contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the field is firmly established with many independent groups and the results are repeated with fermions, spin models and microscopy; recognition after 2001 BEC prize and Chu/Cohen-Tannoudji/Phillips is natural and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller quantum simulation theory candidate (B032).
Whether the achievement is judged as a technique rather than a single discovery.
Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac is genuinely difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84) founded quantum cryptography and is one of the clearest examples of quantum foundations producing a concrete technology; it had a lasting influence on quantum information and underlies commercial and satellite quantum links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, the decisive protocol; Ekert's entanglement-based E91 scheme is a distinct and significant contribution. The credited list contains two spellings of Ekert's name, which I treat as one person, and I propose only Bennett and Brassard to avoid the duplicated string and keep a clean pair, though a fair prize might include Ekert.
assessment.maturity: Mature: QKD has been demonstrated over fibre and satellite links with independent confirmations, and its security theory is established; the 2022 prize honoured Bell-test experiments, so there is some overlap but the topic is distinct. Practical security-proof caveats remain.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert's omission would be seen as unfair.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and quantum information.
Implementation security loopholes limit the maturity of applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics achieved strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms, creating the architecture used by most superconducting quantum processors and enabling quantum-limited readout and control.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf (with Wallraff, Huang and others) proposed and demonstrated the architecture in 2004; Schoelkopf's group is central to the experiments and Blais and Girvin to the theory. The 2025 prize (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) honoured macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this is a related but distinct step.
assessment.maturity: Largely mature: the architecture is reproduced by many groups and drives industrial devices, but with the 2025 prize just awarded in the same field it may be too soon for another circuits prize, and the long-term outcome of superconducting quantum computing is not settled.
uncertainties: Wallraff's experimental role is not in the credited names.
Near-term repetition after the 2025 circuits prize.
Whether the quantum-computing outcome will validate the contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for interferometry showed that quantum noise limits can be beaten, and it is now used in gravitational-wave detectors; the theoretical idea and the experimental realisation both have clear lasting impact in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the 1981 proposal for squeezed-state interferometry; early experimental squeezing came from Slusher's Bell Labs group and Kimble's group (my recollection, not independently verified), and Schnabel's group led the audio-band, GEO600 and LIGO-relevant development. Slusher, Walls and the LIGO squeezing teams are not all credited, so allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature: squeezing is an operating technology in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 with demonstrated sensitivity improvements, but the 2017 gravitational-wave prize already covers the detector, and priority among experimental squeezing groups is complicated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2017 prize on LIGO.
Priority disputes among first experimental squeezing demonstrations.
Four credited names exceed the maximum of three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and provided evidence for cosmic-ray sources such as TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane; the instrumental achievement and scientific opening are major.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Spiering was a driving figure in the AMANDA-IceCube lineage; the large collaboration and earlier DUMAND/Baikal efforts complicate the picture, but a two-person credit is plausible from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: the diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses and KM3NeT/Baikal data, though source identification remains limited and the observational field is still developing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and earlier pioneers beyond the credited names.
Limited source identification so far.
Whether the committee sees the field as sufficiently mature.
